content.comment_body: For my home automation setup, I have one [product_name] [article_no] acting as master and two [article_no] slave modules connected on the network. I need to replace the master with a newer [product_name] [article_no] model. When attempting to transfer the master’s configuration using [product_name] [version_no], I encounter an error: 'PC> [product_name] transmission failure.' Is there a specific method to complete this transfer?

If you’re referring to the [article_no] [product_name] utilized with [product_name] [version_no], you will need the latest [product_name] software, [version_no]. This upgrade is available for free download, but access is export-restricted. Why does downloading export-restricted software require registration, and what personal data is necessary for this process?

Thank you for responding. Yes, it is a [product_name] [version_no] with [article_no], and I'm using the latest version of [product_name], but I continue to experience the issue. Does the device type need to be changed in the software before transferring?
Indeed, your previous module was listed as [product_name] [version_no] in the device selection. The replacement module should appear as [product_name] [version_no] during device selection.
When I attempt to switch the model, I receive a message and the [product_name] [version_no] does not display in the list. 'Failed to load panel.'
Could you confirm that you are using [product_name] [version_no]?
Can you upload the original program from the [product_name] [version_no] with [article_no] as a zip file?
My [product_name] version is [version_no] ([version_no] [date_time]). Zip file is attached. Thanks for your support.

This network project does not contain the [article_no] you mentioned. All three [product_name] modules in the project are [article_no] standard devices. It seems you want to swap the master module for the current [product_name] [version_no], correct?
Yes, the current master module is [article_no], and I intend to replace it with [article_no].

It appears the original project is corrupted. I tried building a new project—see if it works for you. However, I lack the relevant hardware for testing. If the new project also fails, unfortunately you'll need to recreate it completely.
I’ll test it tomorrow and hope for success. Could you clarify what you meant by "damaged"? Thank you for your assistance.
As mentioned, the project is corrupted. You are not alone with this type of issue. Did you load the original project using [product_name] [version_no] and save it?
Hello, it worked well with the file you provided. Thank you for your help. How did you fix the project?

I exported the master module program into a single diagram file, created a new network project, added the two slave modules, and imported the master’s program. Afterwards, I manually configured all inputs and outputs for the master module.
